title: ENARA Deep Learning Simulation v2.0 - pre-registration
note: Simulation of AI students only; not evidence of learning in real humans. This file is locked (hash recorded) before the main experiment is run.
design: Crossed balanced design: each AI student studies 6 outcomes (one per skill area), each in a different one of 6 conditions (Latin-square rotation, seeded). Unit of analysis: student (paired differences). Replications are independent runs with independent seeds; each student x outcome block is used once per replication (no pseudoreplication). Pre-test, immediate post-test, novel-situation transfer, simulated delayed retention (1, 7, 30 days).
primaryOutcome: Immediate learning gain (post - pre proportion correct on independent deterministic assessments), ENARA (A) minus no-teaching control (F).
multipleComparisons: Holm-Bonferroni over the confirmatory family; Benjamini-Hochberg over exploratory contrasts, which are labelled exploratory.
inference: Two-way (student x outcome) cluster bootstrap 95% CIs; sign-flip permutation tests on per-student differences; Hedges g.
decisionRules: A result is reported as supported only if the Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the 95% CI excludes 0. Unfavourable results are reported in full. Failed or incomplete blocks stay in the report.
amendmentBeforeLock: Pre-registered before the main experiment (validation campaigns excluded from it). After validation campaign 1-2 showed chance pre-test imbalance between conditions at n=48, comparisons of A with B, C and E use the pre-adjusted gain (post - pre) instead of raw post. The main experiment has not been run when this file is locked.
analysisUnitNote: Pre-test is taken before teaching on each block; gains are therefore comparable across blocks.
